scope: UIKit native example development; research-only, not model benchmark

model.product: Codex coding assistant in this conversation

incidents.title: Compiler diagnostic wording guessed from property optionality
incidents.observation: The invalid assignment was intentional. The unexpected failure was the matcher expecting String? while the compiler emitted String; the intended failure did not qualify until the matcher was versioned.
incidents.lesson: Derive diagnostic expectations from captured compiler output. Property declaration optionality does not guarantee diagnostic wording. Keep exact toolchain and fail closed for unknown diagnostics.
incidents.evaluation: Ask a model to design a compiler-negative check without supplying the exact message. Score whether it captures and versions actual output rather than guessing or accepting every nonzero exit.

incidents.title: Autorelease timing mistaken for persistent retention
incidents.observation: The first positive suite passed14/15; a weak UILabel reference was still non-nil before draining temporary Objective-C references. Source code did not change. An explicit autorelease boundary made the intended ownership assertion meaningful, and a deliberate retained-element mutant still failed.
incidents.lesson: Separate temporary autorelease lifetime from persistent ownership. A weak-reference assertion needs a controlled observation boundary and a mutation that proves it still detects retained ownership.
incidents.evaluation: Give a failing weak UILabel lifetime assertion and ask for a diagnosis. Penalize claiming an Apple leak, changing production ownership without evidence, or deleting the assertion.

incidents.title: XCTFail was incompatible with the adapter assertion whitelist
incidents.observation: The mutant did invoke the forbidden callback. XCTest summarized XCTFail as "failed - ...", not "XCTAssert...". The conservative adapter therefore returned error/not-assessed. The correction recorded call count and asserted zero; it did not widen the adapter to accept arbitrary failures.
incidents.lesson: Understand the grading contract before authoring assertions. An unclassified failure is not a successful mutant kill. Explicit state/count assertions can be clearer and more machine-verifiable.
incidents.evaluation: Supply the log and whitelist. Require preserving error status and proposing a precise counted assertion; reject counting the original adapter error as a passing check.

incidents.title: Detached font traits disagreed with the receiving label environment
incidents.observation: The suite passed10/11. With automatic font adjustment enabled, observed sizes included17 rather than53,17 rather than15,12 rather than43, and12 rather than11. Passing a separate trait collection to font creation had not configured the receiving label environment.
incidents.lesson: Reason about the receiving UIKit trait environment and automatic adjustment together, not just preferredFont in isolation. Retain exact requested categories and style checks.
incidents.evaluation: Ask for a reusable Dynamic Type label test across categories. Check that it sets and verifies effective traits rather than comparing a detached font against a differently configured label.

incidents.title: Trait override assumed to propagate synchronously
incidents.classification: Model-authored lifecycle/test setup; second attempt in same family
incidents.observation: After assigning traitOverrides, the new effective-category assertion still read large instead of accessibilityXXXL or small. Calling updateTraitsIfNeeded after assignment resolved the setup. All nine style/category combinations remained asserted.
incidents.lesson: Configuration assignment and effective state are different steps. Use the documented synchronous trait update boundary when a deterministic unit assertion requires it; do not add arbitrary sleeps.
incidents.evaluation: Present the failed effective-category assertion. Require a documented update boundary, no UI automation or global preference mutation, and preservation of the expected large/small categories.

incidents.title: Native UIButton role assumed to appear in a headless property getter
incidents.classification: Unsupported oracle about test environment; native observation

before.code:
func testPlayPauseControlMetadataTransitions() {
        let button = UIButton(type: .system)
        MediaConfiguration.configure(button, playing: false)
        XCTAssertEqual(button.title(for: .normal), "Play")
        XCTAssertEqual(button.accessibilityLabel, "Play")
        XCTAssertEqual(button.accessibilityValue, "Paused")
        MediaConfiguration.configure(button, playing: true)
        XCTAssertEqual(button.title(for: .normal), "Pause")
        XCTAssertEqual(button.accessibilityLabel, "Pause")
        XCTAssertEqual(button.accessibilityValue, "Playing")
        XCTAssertTrue(button.accessibilityTraits.contains(.button))
    }

incidents.observation: The direct getter did not contain .button in this headless run. The example now explicitly inserts the trait, so the passing test proves explicit configuration. It does NOT explain the native getter observation or prove a displayed UIButton lacks a button role.
incidents.lesson: Do not equate a headless getter with the assistive-technology representation. Label the correction as a change from an assumed default to an explicit configuration contract; native-default behavior remains a bounded unresolved observation.
incidents.evaluation: Ask why a native UIButton trait assertion fails in a logic test. Reward scope discipline; reject claiming VoiceOver announces no role or that every UIButton must have its role manually added.

incidents.title: Two authored subtitle tracks assumed to mean two selection options
incidents.classification: Model-authored data-model assumption with framework metadata evidence
incidents.observation: AVFoundation returned English, English Forced, Spanish and Spanish Forced. The original count assertion failed4 versus2, including on a diagnostic second run. The final test checks two full and two forced-only variants and both language sets for this pinned fixture. A new forced-only mutant proves language alone is insufficient.
incidents.lesson: Inspect actual options and characteristics. Do not infer one option per authored track or select solely by language. Exact option counts are fixture/runtime observations, not general API guarantees.
incidents.evaluation: Use a natural question about Spanish subtitles selecting incomplete content. Evaluate distinction between full and forced-only options and preserve authored content. Include assets with different option cardinalities so memorizing four does not pass.

incidents.title: Object identity used for a String-valued action category
incidents.classification: Model-authored Swift type error in test code
incidents.observation: Library type-check passed, but the XCTest target did not compile: argument type String expected to be an instance of a class or class-constrained type. Zero tests executed. Replacing === with XCTAssertEqual fixed the authored test; production code was unchanged.
incidents.lesson: Inspect the actual declaration and compile the test target, not just library code. A successful source type-check cannot establish a runnable test suite.
incidents.evaluation: Ask for an edit-category assertion. Check correct value equality and require evidence that tests were discovered and executed.
